text_blocks.snippet: Body fluids and electrolytes are crucial for maintaining overall health and proper bodily functions. Body fluids, primarily water, act as a medium for chemical reactions and transport, while electrolytes, which are minerals with an electrical charge, regulate fluid balance, muscle and nerve function, and other essential processes.
snippet_highlighted_words: Body fluids, primarily water, act as a medium for chemical reactions and transport, while electrolytes, which are minerals with an electrical charge, regulate fluid balance, muscle and nerve function, and other essential processes

list.title: Composition:
list.snippet: Body fluids, mainly water, are distributed both inside cells (intracellular fluid) and outside cells (extracellular fluid).

list.title: Functions:
list.snippet: They act as a medium for chemical reactions, transport nutrients, and remove waste products.

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: Electrolytes are minerals that carry an electrical charge when dissolved in a liquid.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Common electrolytes include sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride, phosphate, and magnesium.

list.title: Functions:
list.snippet: Electrolytes regulate fluid balance, nerve and muscle function, and other vital processes. They also help maintain the body's pH balance.

list.title: Sources:
list.snippet: Electrolytes are obtained through food and beverages, and the kidneys help maintain the proper balance by filtering and excreting excess electrolytes through urine.

list.title: Imbalances:
list.snippet: Electrolyte imbalances can occur due to various factors like illness, excessive sweating, or certain medications, and can lead to various health issues.

list.title: Importance:
list.snippet: Maintaining a balance between body fluids and electrolytes is essential for homeostasis (a stable internal environment).

list.title: Consequences of Imbalance:
list.snippet: Imbalances can disrupt cellular function, affect nerve and muscle activity, and even lead to organ dysfunction.

list.title: Regulation:
list.snippet: The body uses various mechanisms, including hormones and the kidneys, to regulate fluid and electrolyte balance.

list.title: Clinical Relevance:
list.snippet: Nurses and other healthcare professionals need to understand fluid and electrolyte balance to assess patients, identify potential imbalances, and provide appropriate interventions.
